To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
luteinizing-hormone (LH) stimulates the transient and sequential synthesis of epidermal-growth-factor (EGF)-related growth factors in the ovarian follicles.
the EGF-related growth factor amphiregulin is a paracrine mediator of the luteinizing-hormone-induced ovulatory process.
LH stimulation induces transient expression of EGF family members in the follicle, and that EGF family members can recapitulate the LH signal in the follicle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie the ovulatory response of the follicle to LH.
the role of growth factors in the regulation of follicle development, ovulation, and corpus luteum formation.
understanding how the ovary responds to LH stimulation to trigger the final stages of follicular development and oocyte maturing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EGF-like growth factors are mediators of the LH action in the ovulatory follicle.
EGF-like growth factors are mediators of LH action in the ovulatory follicle.
the LH-induced expression of amphiregulin and epiregulin mediates the LH-induced cumulus expansion and that the LH-induced beta-cellulin expression is involved in the LH-induced oocyte maturation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LH receptor is not expressed by cumulus cells, but LH can induce cumulus expansion through the expression of amphiregulin.
EGF family members are the mediators of LH action in the ovulatory follicle.
the LH-induced expression of EGF-related growth factor is the first step in the cascade of events that lead to ovulation in the follicle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LH stimulates the expression of EGF family members in granulosa cells, which in turn stimulate cumulus expansion and meiotic maturation of oocytes.
LH induces the expression of a number of EGF-like proteins that act in a paracrine fashion to induce cumulus expansion.
EGF-like factors can mediate many LH effects in the ovulatory follicle.
